questions.question: Comprehend the concept of local connectivity in convolutional neural networks. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Comprehend the concept of local connectivity in convolutional neural networks. 5 mark
  • Local Connectivity means:Each neuron in the convolutional layer is connected only to a small
  • spatial region (called a receptive field) of the input.
  • For example:
  • o If the input image is 32 × 32
  • o A filter (kernel) size is 3 × 3
  • o Each output neuron looks at only 3 × 3 pixels, not the entire image.
  • Local Connectivity is Needed because Images have spatial structure:
  • o Nearby pixels are strongly related.
  • o Important features (edges, corners, textures) are local patterns.
  • Local connectivity helps the network to Capture local patterns , Reduce number of parameters,
  • Improve computational efficiency,
  • Prevent overfitting

questions.question: Explain how convolutional layers extract features from images. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how convolutional layers extract features from images. 5 mark
  • Convolutional layers extract features by applying learnable filters across the image, generating
  • feature maps that highlight important patterns. By stacking multiple layers, CNNs build a hierarchy
  • of features, enabling accurate image understanding.
  • • Take the input image (as a matrix of pixel values).
  • • Choose a small filter (kernel) (e.g., 3×3).
  • • Place the filter on the image (starting at top-left).
  • • Multiply corresponding values (image × filter).
  • • Add all values → gives one number.
  • • Store the result in the output (feature map).
  • • Slide the filter across the image and repeat.
  • • Form the full feature map after scanning entire image.
  • • Apply activation (ReLU) to keep important features.
  • • Use multiple filters to detect different features (edges, textures, etc.).

questions.question: Explain step-by-step: from QKV projection to weighted sum in attention. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain step-by-step: from QKV projection to weighted sum in attention. 5 mark
  • Start with input embeddings-Convert each word/token into a vector.
  • Create Query, Key, and Value-From each input, generate three vectors:
  • Query → what the word is searching for
  • Key → what the word contains
  • Value → actual information of the word
  • Compare Query with all Keys-Each word checks how related it is to every other word.
  • Get attention scores-These comparisons produce scores showing importance.
  • Scale the scores-Adjust values to keep them stable during training.
  • Apply softmax-Convert scores into probabilities (weights that sum to 1).
  • Multiply weights with Values-Give more importance to relevant words and less to others.
  • Add (sum) the weighted values-Combine them to form the final output for each word.
  • 25901231

questions.question: Describe the role of volumetric data in modern machine learning applications. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of volumetric data in modern machine learning applications.
  • While 2D images represent flat scenes captured by cameras, 3D images (volumetric data) arise
  • in domains such as medical imaging, especially CT (Computed Tomography) scans. A CT scan
  • consists of multiple 2D slices taken along the head-to-foot axis of the human body. When
  • stacked together, these slices form a 3D volume that represents the internal anatomy.
  • In CT imaging, each pixel intensity corresponds to tissue density—from low-density regions like
  • lungs (dark) to high-density structures like bones (bright). These values are computed from how
  • X-rays are attenuated as they pass through the body and are reconstructed using mathematical
  • algorithms. Unlike RGB images, CT data usually has only one intensity channel, similar to
  • grayscale images.Because there is only a single channel, the raw CT data is often stored as a 3D
  • array: D×H×W
  • where:
  • • D = depth (number of slices),
  • • H = height,
  • • W = width.
  • Here, the extra dimension represents physical depth in space, not color information.
  • Volumetric Data as Tensors.From a tensor perspective, volumetric data is not fundamentally
  • different from image data—it simply has one extra dimension. When used in deep learning:
  • • A single volume is represented as C × D × H × W
  • • A batch of volumes is represented as:N×C×D×H×W
  • Medical images are commonly stored in DICOM format. Using tools like imageio.volread, a
  • directory of DICOM slices can be loaded and automatically assembled into a 3D NumPy array.
  • Since PyTorch expects a channel dimension, an additional dimension is added u sing unsqueeze
  • to represent the single intensity channel.Once converted to a floating-point tensor, multiple CT
  • volumes can be stacked along the batch dimension, enabling training and inference with 3D
  • convolutional neural networks.
